name: Lima bean
summary: How Filipino growers raise patani, the climbing lima bean grown along fences and on poles for its green seeds, a staple of pinakbet and ginataang gulay. It is seeded direct and bears for months.
season: Planted at the start of the rains, around May to June, or from October to November. It is often grown along fences and backyard frames.
material: Dry seed from fully mature pods. The big seed is planted direct, sometimes after a short soak.
spacing: Hills about a meter apart along poles, a frame or a fence.
water: Rainfed, with hand watering in long dry spells.
fertilizer: Dried manure or compost at planting, with a side dressing of complete fertilizer (14 14 14) or more manure after about a month.
care: Support for the vines, weeding around the hills, and checking for pod borers and aphids.
harvest: Green pods are picked when the seeds are full but still green, every few days for months. Dry pods give next season's seed.

ways.label: Direct seeded on poles or a fence

steps.title: Dig and add manure
steps.how: Dig the plot or spots along the fence and mix in dried manure or compost.

steps.title: Plant the seed
steps.how: Plant 2 to 3 seeds a hill, with hills about a meter apart, and cover them with 3 to 5 cm of soil.

steps.title: Thin and put up poles
steps.how: Leave the strongest one or two plants and set up poles, a frame or strings to the fence for the vines.

steps.title: Weed
steps.how: Hoe out the weeds around the hills.

steps.title: Feed
steps.how: Side dress complete fertilizer (14 14 14) or more manure around the plants.

steps.title: Watch for pests
steps.how: Check the flowers and pods for pod borers and the leaves for aphids.

steps.title: Pick the green pods
steps.how: Pick the pods when they are plump and the seeds inside are full but still green, every few days.

steps.title: Keep seed pods
steps.how: Leave some pods on the vine to dry for seed.

parts.title: Leave pods on the best vines
parts.how: Stop picking some full, well shaped pods on the strongest, healthiest vines and let them hang until they turn dry and papery.

parts.title: Pick and dry the pods
parts.how: Pick the dry pods before they split, spread them on a mat in the sun until brittle, then break them open and take out the big seeds.

parts.title: Sort and dry the seed
parts.how: Keep the big, plump, unspotted seeds and throw out wrinkled or holed ones. Sun dry them once more, turning them, until they are hard.

parts.title: Store it sealed
parts.how: Keep the seed in a sealed jar or can in a cool, dry place until the next planting. A little dry wood ash mixed in keeps weevils off.

ways.note: Day 85 is about the first picking of green pods. The vine keeps bearing for months.

mistakes: Planting the big seed too deep in wet soil, where it rots.
Letting the pods dry on the vine when green seeds are wanted.
better: Plant fresh, whole seed into moist soil, not soggy soil.
Feed with compost and a side dressing and pick often.
Scout for pod borers at flowering.

watering.traditional: Patani grows along fences and backyard frames, planted with the rains and watered by hand only in long dry spells. Old vines with deep roots bear for months on the rain alone.
watering.method: Hand watering with a can or a hose at the base of each hill, in the early morning or late afternoon.
watering.rainfed: Plant at the start of the rains or from October to November, near a fence or frame where the roots can go deep. Mulch the base of the vine.
watering.dryseason: Bearing vines in the dry months need a watering every few days. Water when the leaves droop in the morning or the soil is dry a finger deep.
watering.wet: Plant on a mound or raised spot so rain drains away, since standing water rots the roots.

schedule.often: Water at planting if the soil is dry, then every day or two until the seedlings are up
schedule.amount: Enough to keep the hill moist, never soggy
schedule.why: The big seed rots in soggy soil but needs moisture to sprout.

schedule.often: Usually the rains are enough. In a dry spell, water when the topsoil dries
schedule.amount: A watering can of about 10 liters shared among a few hills

schedule.often: In dry weeks, water every few days
schedule.amount: Soak the soil around each hill
schedule.why: Dry soil drops the flowers and leaves the pods half full.

critical: Coming up, the first two weeks: keep the hill moist.
Flowering and pod filling: drought drops the flowers and leaves empty pods.

signs.dry: Leaves droop and pale, flowers drop and pods fill poorly.
signs.wet: Yellow leaves and rotting roots and stem base.

better: Mulch the base of the vine so the soil stays moist between waterings.
Water steadily while the vine flowers and fills its pods.
